Implement the `RuntimeErrors` component to handle and display runtime errors in Gatsby's development server error overlay. Ensure it gracefully manages errors without a stack trace and deduplicates identical errors.

*   Implement the `RuntimeErrors` component as a named export in `packages/gatsby/cache-dir/fast-refresh-overlay/components/runtime-errors.js`.
    *   Signature: `RuntimeErrors({ errors, dismiss })`
    *   Parameters:
        *   `errors`: An array of Error objects, each potentially lacking a `stack` property.
        *   `dismiss`: A function to dismiss the overlay.

*   Ensure the component renders the `message` text of each unique error visibly in the DOM.
    *   Handle errors with a `stack` property by rendering their `message` text without crashing.
    *   Handle errors without a `stack` property by rendering their `message` text visibly without throwing an error or crashing.

*   Implement deduplication logic:
    *   Ensure each unique error in the `errors` array is rendered only once, even if the same Error object appears multiple times.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory. The verification system will apply test patches automatically. Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

The implementation is complete. Here's what I changed in `runtime-errors.js`: **1. Deduplication (no longer crashes on missing `stack`)** — The old code did `error.stack.split()` unconditionally, throwing a `TypeError` for stackless errors. Now the dedup key falls back to the Error object's identity when there's no stack (or no location line), so: - Errors thrown from the same location still dedupe by stack line. - The same stackless Error object appearing multiple times renders only once (identity dedup). **2. `getCodeFrameInformationFromError`** — Returns `null` early when `error.stack` is absent, avoiding the throw from `ErrorStackParser.parse()` (which requires a stack). **3. `WrappedAccordionItem`** — Made robust to null code-frame info: - `modulePath?.replace(...)` (optional chaining) instead of `modulePath.replace(...)`, which would have thrown when `moduleId` was undefined. - `useStackFrame(codeFrameInformation ?? {})` — the hook destructures its argument, so it always gets an object, and the hook is still called unconditionally (React rules-of-hooks preserved). - The code-frame UI (file path, "Open in Editor", ``) only renders when code-frame info exists. In all cases `

{error.message}

` is rendered into the DOM, so every unique error's `message` is visible — with or without a stack — and the component never crashes. I did not touch anything under `tests/`.
